q: The Furstenberg boundary of a semisimple Lie group G is a G-space B(G) used in the Zimmer program because:
opts: It is the unique compact G-space
It is the unique measurable G-space with no invariant probability measure (non-amenable)
Every ergodic G-action has a G-equivariant map to B(G), enabling rigidity arguments
exp: Every ergodic G-action (and hence every lattice action that extends) factors onto the Furstenberg boundary via a measurable equivariant map (Furstenberg's boundary theory). This is the key to proving cocycle superrigidity and other rigidity phenomena.
